primitives.verbatim_quote: Method / model Three composable, non-invasive features, each choosable per transaction: - **LV[R] (Recovery):** file-based markers reserve snapshot versions at transaction start (Delta: appended to the log; Iceberg: new path); transaction sublogs + physical/logical undo/redo enable greedy adaptation to concurrent changes instead of aborting.

primitives.name: LakeVilla Complex Transaction Ordering
primitives.verbatim_quote: - **LV[CT] (Complex Transactions):** marker-based conflict and deadlock detection *across all accessed tables*; a client discovering markers on a newly accessed table inherits dependency order; on cycles/timeout, a marker shift inverts the dependency globally.

primitives.breakdown_regime: Deadlock or cycle detection triggers global marker reordering to maintain serializability.

LakeVilla introduces two core primitives—LV[R] for recovery and LV[CT] for complex transactions—that together close a critical gap in lakehouse ACID support. LV[R] uses file-based markers to reserve snapshot versions at transaction start, enabling undo/redo mechanisms that avoid aborts. This is mathematically modeled as a temporal sequence of ordered snapshots S_t, where each M_t marks a consistent view. LV[CT] extends this by constructing a dependency graph D_t over accessed tables, ensuring serializability via marker-order transitivity. When a client accesses a new table, it inherits a partial order from existing markers, resolving conflicts through global inversion on cycle detection. These primitives are composable and optional per transaction, allowing modular application. In GSE’s context, LV[R] aligns with manifest-based atomicity, while LV[CT] enables robust handling of multi-table build dependencies. The system assumes atomic object-store writes and handles non-LakeVilla clients via hidden versions. Failure modes include marker inconsistency under client crashes, which are mitigated via sublog tracking and sweep detection.
